name: The Silver Road
region_detail: An abandoned trade route crossing the outer dunes beyond the regularly traveled caravan roads.
site_type: caravan wreck | Abandoned infrastructure; supernatural sites | Scattered caravan remains and forgotten desert trail.
history: Generations ago, a Qasari caravan carrying precious stones, rare spices, and a sealed chest disappeared while traveling along an older desert route. Surviving accounts describe an unfamiliar star observed shortly before the caravan departed from its expected course. The route subsequently fell into disuse.
current_state: Wind periodically exposes fragments of harness, broken containers, and silver coins bearing the caravan master’s distinctive mark. The scattered remains establish that at least part of the caravan traveled this way, but no bodies or sealed chest have been conclusively identified. Much of the old trail remains buried beneath shifting dunes.
inhabitants: Desert scavengers and occasional treasure seekers. The fate of the caravan’s original members remains undetermined.
danger_level: Moderate due to remoteness, shifting sand, and scarcity of water; supernatural hazards are undetermined.
points_of_interest:
Scattered silver coins; weathered caravan markers; partially buried packing crates; fragments of harness; sheltered rest hollow; traces of a route departing from the old trade road.

Unresolved elements: Whether the caravan was destroyed, diverted, transported elsewhere, or abandoned; The nature of the false star; The location and contents of the sealed chest; Whether the scattered remains lead to a separate destination.
discovery: An abandoned trade route crossing the outer dunes beyond the regularly traveled caravan roads. Sahir Keshan has seen coins bearing the caravan master’s mark. Older Qasari route maps and the testimony of travelers who recovered such coins may narrow the search.
related_records:
Rumor: R-RV-005 — The Lost Qasari Caravan — Direct. The scattered remains are associated with the vanished caravan; the truth of the false-star story is unresolved.

Notable individuals and factions: Sahir Keshan (N-121) — can identify the distinctive coins; Qasari merchant families preserving accounts of the disappearance; Independent desert explorers and treasure seekers.
